summary: The story people's own clothes (StoryWalker.costume / person_look; StoryActor.make for a named fighter; WreckFall's two men), by their story tag. Each costume's outfit goes over the person's look slot by slot, as a look's "outfit" key (PlayerOutfit: {slot: {id, colors}}; colours per zone index, or {"preset": a name of the garment's catalog extra.presets}, the other keys over it; the id "-" takes a slot off). A garment this build does not have leaves its slot to the basic dress. hair_style, when set, is the look's hair style. by_mission (2026-10-03): {mission id: {slot: {id, colors}}} worn over the costume while that mission lasts (StoryWalker.person_look's mission; the people effect passes its mission): Margaretha's jacket from the late-October warning on and her hooded cloak for the night of the raid. The outfits are the clothes agents' assembled and rendered ones (2026-10-03): the Rauchs, Jost and Vane the settlers' set; Leclerc the Canadian militiaman's with a blue capot, so he is the one picked out at the camp; Captain Ithel and Rook the Drift set's (Rook's Act 2 dress, glow dead under our sky: he wears it at the wreck and on his walk). No Native person's clothes here (the consultation rule).

margaretha._note: In shift sleeves, stays and apron at work about the farm in early October; out of doors in the late October and November missions she wears her jacket, and on the night of the raid (3 a.m., 12 November) her hooded cloak over it.

vane._note: 2026-10-03: his signature is the long madder-red waistcoat with gilt buttons under the open skirts of his snuff coat and the gold-laced hat (at 20 m he was the farmers' brown ditto suit); silver buckles.

ithel._note: 2026-10-03: a captain's gold-laced cocked hat and a white stock (bare-headed in an open collar he read as a deckhand); the sail cloak's fur collar lies down on the shoulders, its battens unlit: his one glow is his coat's cording, fading with him.

rook._note: 2026-10-03: his tow shirt checked with slate grey (the tow-on-tow check read at 20 m as bare arms under the cape: its mean is close to his skin).
